questions.stem: Why is the precipitate washed with distilled water after filtering?

options.text: To remove soluble impurities trapped in the precipitate
To make the precipitate change colour

questions.explanation: After filtering, the precipitate contains traces of the soluble salts from the solution. Washing with distilled water removes these soluble impurities while the insoluble salt remains on the filter paper, giving a pure product.

questions.stem: To make lead iodide by precipitation, which pair of reactants should be used?

options.text: Lead nitrate solution and potassium iodide solution

questions.explanation: Lead iodide (PbI₂) is insoluble, so it must be made by precipitation. Both reactants must be soluble: lead nitrate (soluble, as all nitrates are) and potassium iodide (soluble, as all potassium salts are). Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) + 2KI(aq) → PbI₂(s) + 2KNO₃(aq).
